stem.text: Let \( h(x) = 2 x^{3} - 9 x^{2} - 5 \). Using the second derivative test where it applies, determine whether h has a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at \( x = 3 \) and at \( x = 1 \).

answer_key.label: At \( x = 3 \), h has a relative minimum because \( h'(3) = 0 \) and \( h''(3) = 18 > 0 \); at \( x = 1 \), h has no relative extremum because \( h'(1) = -12 \ne 0 \).

worked_solution.text: Differentiate: \( h'(x) = 6 x^{2} - 18 x \), which factors as \( h'(x) = 6 x \left(x - 3\right) \).
\( h'(3) = 0 \), so \( x = 3 \) is a critical point, while \( h'(1) = -12 \ne 0 \), so \( x = 1 \) is not.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points are zeros of the first derivative
second derivative evaluated at the critical point

worked_solution.text: By the second derivative test h has a relative minimum at \( x = 3 \). At \( x = 1 \) the first derivative is not zero, so h has no relative extremum there and the test does not apply.

options.label: At \( x = 3 \), h has a relative maximum because \( h'(3) = 0 \) and \( h''(3) = 18 > 0 \); at \( x = 1 \), h has no relative extremum because \( h'(1) = -12 \ne 0 \).
options.derivation: the sign convention of the test reversed, so a negative second derivative is read as a minimum and a positive one as a maximum

options.derivation: the second derivative test also applied at x = 1, where the first derivative is not zero, and the sign of the second derivative there read as a classification
